source.title: Neuron-based Pruning of Deep Neural Networks with Better Generalization using Kronecker Factored Curvature Approximation

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether a Hessian spectral-radius penalty affects validation accuracy after neuron pruning, using ablations. It does not test the claim versions' specified gap or generalization measurements.
record.gate_note: The Taylor-versus-HGNP comparisons are comparisons of the study's own method with another method and are not extracted as rows. The ablation results compare validation accuracy after pruning with and without parts of the spectral-radius method.
record.test_reason: The study uses the premise that flatter minima generalize better to design a pruning algorithm and reports validation accuracy and computational performance. It does not test V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation measure or its association with train–test gaps, or any other claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they claim HGNP produces compact networks with flatter minima, better generalization, and faster inference through neuron pruning. Their validation comparisons favor HGNP in many pruning settings, but not uniformly; its accuracy–sparsity AUC is slightly worse than Taylor for ResNet-18/Birds. The paper does not directly report achieved flatness measurements or train–test gaps.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes integrated neuron pruning and training with a K-FAC-approximated spectral-radius penalty; its experiments concern pruning performance rather than the claim versions' tests of generalization gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: The ablation comparison reports that the full method is consistently better below 58% sparsity on AlexNet trained on Flowers.

fits_no_version.finding: Full HGNP achieves higher validation accuracy than either spectral-radius component ablation on AlexNet/Flowers below the paper's 58% retained-weight fraction; exact accuracies and uncertainty are not supplied in the text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Including the spectral-radius component in both training and neuron selection improves validation accuracy in this tested pruning setting.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network
record.problems: The relevant ablation results are shown only in a figure; the paper gives no numerical values or uncertainty estimates for them. The finding is from one architecture and dataset.
record.rows_left_out: Taylor-versus-HGNP comparisons in Sections 4.1 and 4.4 were left out because they compare the study's proposed method with another method rather than isolate a claim version's object. Figure-only ablation accuracies are retained only as figure-only values because exact numbers are not stated.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Widening networks beyond zero training error and measuring subsequent test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Effects of adding or removing dropout on held-out error.

Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with measured train–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. The spectral-radius penalty and validation-accuracy ablations do not measure these.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: No claim-version verdict is warranted. Pruning neurons does not test removing memorized examples, and varying retained network size during pruning does not establish V2's width effect beyond interpolation.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, measured train-test gaps, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized examples and the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on Flowers dataset
rows.operation_detail: Ablation 1 sets μ = 0 during training, while retaining the complete loss function for neuron selection; validation accuracy is compared with full HGNP.
rows.note: The text says full HGNP is consistently better below 58% sparsity; exact accuracies are not stated.
rows.check: This is a component ablation of the proposed pruning method, not a test of a claim version; 'reversed' is therefore inappropriate. The stated direction is correct: full HGNP has higher validation accuracy below 58% retained-weight fraction. Training from scratch is unsupported: Section 4.3 does not specify initialization, and the main AlexNet/Flowers experiment uses ImageNet initialization. The paper's 'sparsity' denotes the fraction of weights retained.

source_check.correct: AlexNet uses ImageNet-trained parameters except for a randomly initialized final fully connected layer; training from scratch is not the reported Flowers setup.
